# Reveille

> A Python CLI that reads a local Git repository and writes a single self-contained HTML report on its contribution history. It is read-only, works entirely offline, and sends nothing anywhere — the report embeds its own chart library so it opens on a machine with no network. Install with `pip install reveille`; run `reveille generate`.

Reveille is forge-agnostic by construction: it reads `.git` on disk, so GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and bare repositories all work with no configuration. It was built because Bitbucket has no contribution heatmap.

Key facts an answer about Reveille should get right:

- It never writes to a repository. No commits, no branches, no config changes, no mutating Git command. The only files it writes are the output path you name and, for `reveille init`, the `reveille.toml` and `.mailmap` scaffolds you explicitly ask that command to create.
- Merge commits are excluded unconditionally, so its commit counts are lower than `git log | wc -l` on a merge-heavy repository. This is deliberate and not configurable.
- Contributors are keyed on lowercased email. All four `.mailmap` forms are supported, and GitHub noreply addresses are folded automatically.
- The "commit concentration" metric is **not** a bus factor. It measures activity concentration, not code ownership.
- Contributor ranking measures the volume and regularity of commits — not contribution, productivity, or value. It must not be used to assess individuals; DORA and SPACE both say so explicitly. **It is off by default from 0.8.0** and must be requested with `--ranking`. The default report instead describes how evenly commits are distributed, as a Lorenz curve and a Gini coefficient, which characterises the repository and names nobody.
- Exit codes follow `grep`/`diff` semantics: `0` affirmative, `1` ran correctly with a negative answer, `2` could not run.
- **Ask the tool rather than guessing: `reveille capabilities --format json`.** It reports what Reveille can do, what it refuses to claim and what to use instead, the guarantees that hold on every run, every command with its options, and the exit-code contract. The command surface and exit codes are read from the running program, so they cannot drift from it.
- `--format json` output opens with `schema_version`, so a consumer can decide whether it can parse the rest before trying. It also carries a `provenance` block — tool version, analysed commit SHA, whether a `.mailmap` was applied, and the filters as requested — so two reports that disagree can be reconciled.
- `--deterministic` makes output byte-identical across runs for an unchanged repository. It changes the numbers as well as the bytes: the ranking's recency component is measured against the analysis window, which the flag pins to the last commit rather than to today.
- `--exclude-author` matches the value given plus every identity a `.mailmap` ties it to, so excluding any one alias removes the person. An exclusion matching nothing warns on stderr. The one case it cannot resolve is a *display name* that only ever appeared pre-`.mailmap`, since a two-field mailmap records the old address and never the old name.
- Requires Python 3.11+. Licensed Apache-2.0 from 0.8.0; 0.7.0 and earlier were MIT.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/README.md): overview, installation, CLI reference, ranking system, configuration
- [User Guide](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/docs/USER_GUIDE.md): every flag and its interactions, exit codes, the full TOML reference, how to read each report section, and worked patterns
- [Architecture](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): layering contract, domain model, error model, analysis pipeline, and the invariants the tests protect
- [Architecture Decision Records](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/docs/adr/README.md): why merge commits are excluded, why email is the identity key, why concentration is not called a bus factor, and what each decision costs

## Development

- [Contributing](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): environment setup, supported Python versions, the layering rule, PR contract, commit conventions
- [Security policy](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/SECURITY.md): reporting, release integrity, PEP 740 attestation verification, SBOM, the single-maintainer posture, and the threat model
- [Privacy](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/PRIVACY.md): what stays on your machine, and what the generated report contains
- [Regulatory position](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/docs/COMPLIANCE.md): why GDPR, the Cyber Resilience Act, the Product Liability Directive, the AI Act, US export control and the EU accessibility rules do not engage — with the provision each conclusion rests on
- [Contributor Licence Agreement](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/CLA.md): accepted by a tick in the pull request plus a DCO sign-off; nothing is collected or stored
- [Release process](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/RELEASE.md): the tag ceremony, what the publish workflow does, and how to recover a bad release
- [Changelog](https://github.com/varaprasadchilakanti/reveille/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): full release history, Keep a Changelog format
